verdict: Better than r1 in places, but still not at the fern bar (mean about 5.7). The scores are unchanged after this check. Window is now a usable shot. Dawn reclines into a reclined backrest and her upper back touches it. Her profile, ear and bun are sculpted, and her right hand lies on her left in her lap. But the light barely picks her out. Measured graded L*: the lit planes of her face average about 52 (brow 62, peak 71 on the nose and brow, the frame's maximum). The linen cover right behind her head is about 48-50 and the lit near side of the window reveal about 48. Both read cool, so the window fill and the sky light them, not her warm lamp. Aisle still reads as an empty cabin with a pale egg in it. Her head is about 85 px tall and seen almost straight from behind, with no shoulders, and the bun lit from the side makes the back of the head read like a face. Her head averages about L* 40 (crown 49, peak 66). The two blank screens are hard-edged rectangles at about L* 42-43 across their whole face, so by area they are brighter than she is. The near one is low and right of centre, about 150x83 px, on the aisle seat of her own row. The covers on her own seat and on the seat in front of her sit at her value (about 40). The lamp's scallop on the bin and wall above her (L* 74) is the frame's peak. The galley at the vanishing point is black (L* about 3), not the glow the stage describes. Half the frame is under luma 20. The four passengers do not read at the graded level: in a brightened raw, only one head and one dark torso show. Over is a clean night sky, but Dawn no longer reads. Her head is about 24 degrees off the lens axis, and only its near edge enters the lower-right corner, as a soft blur at about L* 8. The shot plays as an insert with no point of view. The winglet is a near-flat dark cut-out (L* 6-9) with a squared top that reads as a tail fin. The strobe is a small bead on the horizon airglow band, about 10 px above the band's peak. That band is the brightest thing in the window (L* 50-53). The wing's top skin (L* 34-37) has no value separation from the hazy deck just beneath it (33-36). The cloud deck is darker than the sky above (about 15 vs 24) but nearly flat inside itself (5th-95th percentile 11-21), with no cell structure, so it reads like calm water or fog. There is no text, lettering, logo or livery anywhere, and red is correctly gone from the wing. Renders are clean, with no fireflies or clipping, but there is no white point outside the strobe's 8 px core (aisle peaks at L* 74, window at 71).
answers: WINDOW, Dawn's recline: it reads now. The trunk slopes back from the hips (the shoulders sit well aft of the hips), the upper back lies on the reclined backrest, and the seat cushion takes her weight. Two weaknesses. (1) The head stays upright on a long vertical neck, so the posture reads as sitting up alert rather than resting back. Let the head lean back a little toward the headrest (head 'down' 10 -> about 6) so the bun or the back of the skull meets the cover with a contact shadow. rigged.pose_figure takes only down and turn, so any roll toward the window needs a direct rotation on the head bone. (2) At the graded level the jacket is a near-black mass (L* about 8-9) against a near-black seat (about 6), so only the neck and hand carry the recline. WINDOW, gaze: correct. Head 34, neck 16 and chest 8 add up to about 58 degrees, close to the 60-65 degrees needed to look at the glass. Her eye line meets the upper-left of the pane. Her nose is only about 25-30 px from the reveal ring in the frame, so at a glance she can look as if she is studying the window frame. Turning the head 4-6 degrees further, or framing about 30 px more air in front of her face, would make it read as looking through the glass. WINDOW, hand contact: the right hand rests on the back of the left with curled fingers, and the contact is believable in the raw. In the graded frame the upper hand is about L* 30-44, and the lower hand is about 10 and nearly lost. Both hands sit far forward on the thigh, near the knee, their lowest point about 40-50 px above the bottom edge, which is cramped. Slide them 6-8 cm back along the thigh. KEY_AIM['window'] aims at chest height (z 1.035), not at the lap. The hands sit in the soft edge of its 58-degree cone, about 19 degrees off its axis, which is why they are a stop and a half under the face. AISLE, do the practical and the linen keep attention on her? No. Her head (L* about 40 mean, 66 max) is not the brightest thing in frame. The screens' flat faces are 42-43, and the lamp's scallop on the bin and sidewall above her peaks at 74. The covers on her own seat and on the seat in front of her are about 40, her value. Covers further off step down to about 16-25 but still repeat pale shapes across the rows. The two blank screens (row 5 and row 6 aisle seats of block 0) are crisp, cool, hard-edged rectangles right of centre, and they pull the eye first. Her reading light reads as a bright scallop on the bin and sidewall rather than as a pool on her, and the haze gives no visible cone. The deepest point of the frame, the galley, is black. OVER, wing, strobe and cloud separation: the winglet silhouette against the sky is strong (L* about 9 vs 25). The wing's top skin does not separate from the deck by value (about 34-37 vs 33-36 just beneath it), only by its thin edges. The winglet has no thickness and no edge light, only a slight curve at its root, and with its squared top it reads as a tail fin. It is backlit because build() sets moon_dir from tip_dir, the camera-to-tip direction, which puts the moon behind the winglet and the face the camera sees in shadow. Only the last few metres of wing show, so it does not reach. The strobe sits on the airglow band, about 10 px (0.2 degrees) above its peak. Its core reaches L* 88 over about 8 px, but the halo reads as a glossy bead, not a light. The deck is about 15 against a sky of about 24 above it, but it has no cells, breaks or moonlit tops (5th-95th percentile only 11-21), so it reads as fog or calm sea. About half the frame is blurred reveal, which reads as a keyhole. With only an unreadable edge of her head in the lower-right corner, the shot has no point of view.

fixes.problem: The two glowing seat-back screens in her own block (flat faces at L* 42-43, about 150x83 and 107x58 px) outshine her head (about 40) and are the first thing the eye finds.
fixes.fix: Lower M['screen_on'] strength in aircraft_cabin_mats.materials() from 0.9 to about 0.3. The strength in each LIT entry only scales that screen's spill lamp, not its glowing face, so LIT cannot dim one screen on its own. The blank screens are part of the set's designed light (stage docstring; framed on purpose in commit 36dc4ae), so dim them rather than delete them. If the near screen in her own row still pulls first, move that one LIT entry to a row further forward. Target: every screen under L* 25 in the graded frame, and Dawn's head the only value above about L* 45 outside the lamp.

fixes.problem: Her reading lamp paints the bin and sidewall (a scallop at frame 435,60, L* 74, the frame's peak) and the covers next to her about as much as her (crown about 49). There is no visible cone and no pool.
fixes.fix: In TRIMS['aisle'], take spill from 1.45 to 0.5. Narrow reading_spill's spot size from 150 to about 90 degrees so it stops painting the bin and the wall above the window. Raise the 'lamp haze' density in build() from 0.135 to about 0.3 (aisle only, as now) so a faint warm beam runs from the lens down onto her head. KEY_AIM['aisle'] already aims the key at her head and seat top with a 60-degree cone, so leave its size. If the pool's rim lands on the covers beside her, pull the aim 3-4 cm toward her head.

fixes.problem: Dawn is an 85 px pale egg seen almost straight from behind. With no shoulders and the bun lit from the side, the back of her head reads like a face or a mannequin head.
fixes.fix: Do not move AISLE_CAM forward to about (-1.25, 2.95). Because she is turned to port toward the glass, that puts the lens within about 10 degrees of straight behind her head, which shows only the back of the head and the bun. At 35 mm it would also put the aisle's vanishing point and the galley out of frame, since the aisle line would be about 50 degrees right of her. A lost profile (ear, jaw and cheek line catching the warm key) needs the line from the lens to her head well off her back line. Keep the 30 mm framing, which holds both her and the galley. Then either turn her further to the glass in this shot (head turn 34 -> about 50; the pose is built once for every camera, so this needs build() to know the camera), or move the camera one or two rows aft along the aisle with a 40-45 mm lens to hold her size, and re-aim so the galley stays in frame. Her own seat back and the middle seat hide her shoulders from any standing height, and lowering the camera hides more of her, so do not chase the shoulders. Check that the bun is in shadow or rim-lit, not front-lit as a disc.

fixes.problem: The linen headrest covers sit at her stone value next to her (about L* 40 beside her head in the aisle shot, 48-50 behind her face in the window shot) and repeat pale shapes across the rows. They also look like rigid foam blocks, not cloth.
fixes.fix: In aircraft_cabin_mats.cover_cloth, darken the default rgb from (0.30, 0.31, 0.325) to about (0.15, 0.155, 0.165) and keep the bump and crumple. In aircraft_cabin_set.cover_cloth, add a sag along the front fold (lower the middle by 1-1.5 cm) and a slightly uneven hem so the cover reads as draped cloth. Target: covers at least 1 stop under her skin in every camera.

fixes.problem: Her lit face (about L* 52, brow 62, peak 71) is barely above the cool linen right behind her head (48-50) and the lit near side of the window reveal (about 48). The light does not pick her out.
fixes.fix: Both surfaces read cool (more blue than red), so window_fill and the sky light them, not the warm spill. Link window_fill to the 'dawn only' collection, as face_fill already is, or narrow its spread from 100 to about 60 degrees, so it stops lighting the cover and the reveal. Cutting spill from 0.55 to 0.25 in TRIMS['window'] is a smaller, secondary trim. Raise fill from 0.4 to 0.75 (face_fill, linked to Dawn only). Target graded L*: face planes about 55-65 with a 75-80 highlight on the cheek or brow, and the headrest cover and the reveal at or under about 35.

fixes.problem: Her head is about 24 degrees off the lens axis. Only its near edge enters the lower-right corner, as a soft blur at L* about 8 that does not read as her, so the shot is an insert of a wing with no point of view. About half the frame is blurred reveal.
fixes.fix: Bring the back of her head in from the lower right, where it already is, not from the left. Pan the aim a few degrees right and down toward HEAD, or widen from 100 mm to about 60-70 mm, so the back of her head and the bun fill the lower-right third as a soft, readable silhouette and the wing and strobe sit left of centre in the pane. At 60 mm and f/16 her head's blur drops from about 120 px to about 35 px. Check that her lamp ('over' key trim 1.6) gives the head a warm rim, and add one if it does not. A wider lens also shows more reveal, so check again that the reveal blur no longer dominates.

fixes.problem: The strobe sits on the horizon airglow, about 10 px above the band's peak, and the band is the brightest thing in the window (L* 50-53). The strobe reads as a glossy bead. The horizon outshines the strobe and the wing, and the wing's top skin has the same value as the haze beneath it.
fixes.fix: Lower the wing so the strobe sits on the darker deck, as the camera note asks ('under the horizon'). The strobe sits about 0.44 m above WING_TIP.z (0.35 m of tip flex plus the 0.09 m mount), so moving WING_TIP z from -1.03 to -2.1 puts it only about 1.6 degrees under the horizon, still in the haze band (L* about 33). About -2.6 to -3.0 puts it 2.5-3 degrees under, on deck values of about 15-20, and lays the wing's top skin against the dark deck too. Lower root_z in exterior() with it (the root is at -2.0), or the wing will droop. fx_over follows WING_TIP; check that the aim still holds the tip in the pane. In aircraft_cabin_mats.sky, darken the airglow band colour from (0.128, 0.143, 0.18) to about (0.08, 0.09, 0.115) and the horizon haze from (0.05, 0.056, 0.07) to about (0.032, 0.036, 0.046). Raise M['nav_white'] strength from 12 to about 60 so the core clips to white over 3-5 px. Enlarge the navlight_halo radius from 0.16 to 0.35, and lower the halo material's falloff power from 5 to 3 with strength 0.65 -> 1.0, so it blooms instead of reading as a sphere.

fixes.problem: The winglet is a flat dark cut-out with a squared top and a sharp corner at the wing, so it reads as a tail fin. It is backlit because moon_dir is taken from the camera-to-tip direction. Only the tip of the wing shows.
fixes.fix: In aircraft_cabin_set.exterior, taper the last winglet ring's chord from 0.8 to about 0.45 and rake it back from 1.6 to 1.9. Add a blend ring at t=0.15 (up about 0.06-0.09, out -0.12, back about 0.08-0.11, chord 2.4) so the root curves. The face the camera sees is the winglet's inboard face, so for a thin sheen on it (L* 20-30) the moon must come from the fuselage side: moon_dir needs a positive x, e.g. about (0.3, 0.6, 0.6). A direction like (-0.55, 0.25, 0.45) would still leave that face dark. Alternatively, keep the moon and add a faint second sun, linked to the exterior collection, from the inboard side. The window opening, not the lens, limits how much wing shows, so a wider lens alone will not make it reach.

fixes.problem: The cloud deck is a near-uniform grey (about L* 15, 5th-95th percentile 11-21) with no cell structure, so it reads like water or fog.
fixes.fix: In aircraft_cabin_mats.sky, change the deck mix from gaps (0.006, 0.007, 0.010) and tops (0.024, 0.028, 0.036) to about (0.003, 0.0035, 0.005) and (0.042, 0.048, 0.060). Raise the cloud noise scale from 0.9 to about 2.2, and tighten cells from maprange(0.4, 0.72) to (0.48, 0.62) for defined cell edges and dark gaps. Brighten the tops toward the moon's azimuth with a dot(dir, moon_dir) term (the moon direction has to be passed into sky()), so the deck has one lit side. Target: cloud tops L* 25-30, gaps L* 6-10, and the sky above at or under its current ~24.

fixes.problem: The galley at the vanishing point is black (L* about 3), so the depth of the cabin dies where the eye goes. The passengers do not read at the graded level, so the 'occupied' night flight reads as an empty aircraft.
fixes.fix: Raise the galley trim in TRIMS['aisle'] from 0.45 to 1.6 (it trims the galley_light area lamps), and M['galley'] strength from 0.58 to 1.0 (the glowing galley wall behind the curtain), so the curtain gap reads as a soft cool glow (L* 22-30) under the blank sign (about L* 28-30 now). Pax1 and Pax3 already sit in the aisle seats near the camera's line, (DAWN_ROW+2, 1, 0) and (DAWN_ROW+4, 0, 2), but their dark suits and low heads vanish. Give them less lean (8 instead of 12-13) and let their heads loll 15-20 degrees into the aisle (a head-bone roll; pose_figure has only down and turn), so their heads rise above the cover line and catch the cove light at L* 15-25: present, but well under Dawn.

fixes.problem: Her head is upright on a reclined trunk. Her hands sit far forward at the knee, about 40-50 px above the frame bottom, and the lower hand is lost in shadow.
fixes.fix: In build(), change the head in upper from (10, 34) to about (6, 38), so the head leans back a little toward the cover and turns a touch further to the glass. Any roll needs a direct head-bone rotation. In settle_dawn_lap, place the stacked hands 6-8 cm further back along the thighs. KEY_AIM['window'] (0.01, 0.10, 1.035) aims at chest height, so the hands sit in the soft edge of its cone, and moving them back brings them only a few degrees further in. If they still sit low, widen the window key from 58 to about 64 degrees rather than lowering the aim, which would take light off her face. Target: the lower hand's knuckles at L* 25 or more and the upper hand at about 40-45.
